timeline.event: Beatrix Potter creates pencil and watercolor painting of Dalguise gardens.
Potter paints 'Fly agaric', an example of her growing sophistication in rendering texture.
First meeting between Beatrix Potter and Charles McIntosh on October 29 at Heath Park.
Beatrix writes picture letter to Eric Moore featuring Mr. Jeremy Fisher.
Potter family's last summer holiday in Scotland at Lennel House.
Beatrix and uncle Henry Roscoe visit Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew in May.
Beatrix Potter paints 'Rain: August in the Lake District'.
Beatrix sends illustration 'A Dream of Toasted Cheese' to uncle Henry Roscoe.
Spring holiday in Tenby, Wales; writes letters to Moore girls.
Success of 'The Tale of Peter Rabbit' leads Potter to buy back Mr. Jeremy Fisher drawings.
Works on 'The Pie and the Patty-Pan', 'The Tale of Two Bad Mice', and 'The Tale of Tuppenny' in Hastings.
Publication of 'The Tale of Benjamin Bunny'.
Death of fiancé Norman Warne during stay at Llanbedr, Wales.
Paints 'Autumnal Landscape' in plein air style.
Photograph taken of Beatrix Potter with William Heelis.
W.P.K. Findlay uses 59 of Potter's fungi illustrations in the fungi volume of Wayside and Woodland series.
Scottish mycologist Dr. Mary Noble attributes fungi drawings at Perth Museum to Beatrix Potter.
